Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). - 1 (F6 et G1) et 4 (lecture d'A3) : différées par J2 (forme forte de F6, G1', A3 strict) ;
- 2 (autorités détenues inexerçables, cycles de détenteurs) : différée par J2, sous le nom `NoLock` (« auto-blocage »), selon la lecture de ce rapport ; G2 et `NoOrphan` restent tels quels.

Restent ouvertes la question 5 de la passe 5 (`available` et `issued` dans l'entrée) et la question 13 de la passe 2 (`WF3` dans la spécification).

Questions nouvelles :

1. **Isomorphisme ordonné ou non ordonné** ((c) 1, constat 1).
   - **Constat.** Dans `sq1` (`transfer_shape_ordered`), la structure 0 a pour enfants une feuille puis une structure à deux champs ; la structure 5 a les mêmes enfants dans l'ordre inverse. Les deux arbres sont isomorphes sans ordre, pas avec ordre. Le transfert de 0 dans 5 est rejeté, par la seule clause `SameShape` : le théorème énonce `SameShape sq1.P 0 5 → TransferPre K0 sq1 0 5`. Le jumeau, une structure 10 de même ordre, est accepté.
   - **Contournement.** Champ par champ (1 dans 9, 2 dans 6), les formes concordent. Mais par définition de `transferEff`, ne suit un transfert que ce qui est détenu ou possédé dans la source : ce que détient ou possède la structure 0 elle-même ne suit que le transfert de 0. Ce point n'a pas de témoin.
   - **L'autre lecture n'est pas complète.** Sans ordre, « la partie correspondante » n'est pas unique dès que deux enfants ont la même forme. Dans `pf0`, les champs 1, 2 de 0 et 4, 5 de 3 sont des feuilles : 1↔4 et 1↔5 sont deux isomorphismes. Où passent les autorités et les emplacements possédés dépendrait de ce choix. La spécification ne donne pas d'identité de champ (`kind` n'est pas interprété). C6, cité en passe 4 ((n) 3, point 2), dit que la forme ne fixe ni l'alignement ni la disposition.
   - **Question.** Faut-il garder l'ordre des indices comme identité des champs, ou donner une règle de correspondance pour l'isomorphisme non ordonné ?
2. **J1, puces 2 et 3, pour un `issue` vers une feuille de la valeur arène** (constat 2).
   - **Constat.** Dans `issue_into_arena_value`, la valeur arène 0 a les champs 1 et 2, tous deux écrits avant `newArena`. Le champ 1 est transféré dans une autre feuille et devient `Moved`. Un `issue` vers 1 satisfait toutes les clauses de la puce 2 : il est accepté et 1 redevient `Init`. L'initialisation de la valeur arène change, contre la puce 3. Seul le chemin par `transfer` a un témoin ; `endUse` laisserait de même une feuille non `Init`, sans témoin.
   - **Question.** Faut-il :
     - rejeter un `issue` dont la destination est une feuille de la valeur arène, ce que la puce 2 ne dit pas ;
     - lire la puce 3 comme « l'effet d'`issue` n'écrit aucune autre feuille de la valeur arène », ce que fait le module ;
     - ou interdire de sortir une partie de la valeur arène tant que l'arène vit ?

## (f) Conflits avec `formal/DESIGN.md`

Inchangés depuis la passe 2 ((f) 1 à 3).

## (g) Verdicts des cas d'épreuve

Chaque verdict est vérifié par `decide` sur la précondition de l'opération en cause. Les relations sont déterministes (`*_det`) : le verdict contraire ne peut pas être dérivé.

Tous les cas des passes 1 à 7 sont rejoués par le build, sauf ceux retirés avec leur état ((d) 1, (p)). Sur les 364 `example` de la passe 7, 342 sont inchangés, 22 retirés, et 16 ajoutés ; les verdicts changés sont en (p).

Nouveaux cas de la tâche (sections « Leaves made `Init` without a write » et « New cases of pass 8 (J1) » du module). Chaque état est atteint depuis `S3.init []` par des pas de `Reachable`.

| Cas | Attendu | Obtenu | Théorème |

| t1'. Jumeau : champs 2 et 3 écrits, structure 1 transférée dans la structure 4 de même forme (`vt2`, `vt3`), puis lecture du champ 6 | `ok`, `ok` | `ok`, `ok` | idem |

Code, docstrings, commentaires, messages de commit en anglais. Rapport en français.

J1. Forme des destinations (garantie 3 de la charte).

Un agrégat partiellement initialisé se transfère champ par champ.
  - `issue` : la destination est une feuille non `Init` qui ne détient aucune autorité active ; seule cette feuille passe à `Init`.
  - `issue` et `reset` ne changent pas l'initialisation de la valeur arène ; `newArena` exige les feuilles du détenteur de `internal` toutes `Init`.

Tout ce que J2 diffère ; pool de handles ; jalon 2 ; concurrence ; flot de contrôle ; suspension ; `defer` ; obligation de libération ; syntaxe ; corpus MM3-H complet.

Zéro `sorry` ; `#print axioms` au plus {propext, Quot.sound} ; aucun `noncomputable` ; `lake build` sans avertissement ; docstrings citant la clause ou l'arbitrage ; rien d'inventé ; aucun énoncé affaibli, tout changement justifié ; revue adverse centrée sur J1 : tout autre chemin vers une feuille `Init` jamais écrite, et tout transfert légal rejeté à tort par la condition de forme ; contre-exemples conservés.

import Ern.MM03
open Ern.MM03

def PreNoShape (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
  HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
  (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) ∧
  AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff s src dst)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (PreNoShape k s src dst) := by unfold PreNoShape; infer_instance

/-- Is `PreNoShape` exactly `TransferPre` minus `SameShape`? -/
example (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    TransferPre k s src dst ↔ PreNoShape k s src dst ∧ SameShape s.P src dst := by
  unfold TransferPre PreNoShape; simp only [and_assoc]

/-- struct 0 = {1 leaf, 2 = {3, 4}} owning the storage 11 (allocated with owner 0);
struct 5 = {6 = {7, 8}, 9 leaf}; 10 the allocator value. -/
def zo0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0),
  (some 2, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (some 5, none, 0), (some 6, none, 0), (some 6, none, 0),
  (some 5, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def zo1 : S3 := write3Eff zo0 [10]
def zo2 : S3 := allocEff zo1 10 0 [(none, none, 0)]
def zo3 : S3 := write3Eff zo2 [1, 3, 4]
def zo4 : S3 := transferEff zo3 1 9
def zo5 : S3 := transferEff zo4 2 6
theorem order_rejects_owned :
    Reachable K0 [] zo5 ∧ (zo3.P[11]?).map (·.owner) = some (.place 0) ∧
      (zo3.A[3]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place 0) ∧
      PreNoShape K0 zo3 0 5 ∧ ¬ SameShape zo3.P 0 5 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 5 zo3 .reject ∧
      ((transferEff zo3 0 5).P[11]?).map (·.owner) = some (.place 5) ∧
      TransferStep K0 1 9 zo3 (.ok zo4) ∧ TransferStep K0 2 6 zo4 (.ok zo5) ∧
      (∀ l ∈ footprint zo5.P 0, zo5.I l = .moved) ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint zo5.P 5, zo5.I l = .init) ∧
      (zo5.P[11]?).map (·.owner) = some (.place 0) ∧ (zo5.A[3]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place 0) := by
  have r1 : Reachable K0 [] zo1 := .write (.enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)))
    (show Write3Step 2 [10] zo0 (.ok zo1) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable K0 [] zo2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep K0 10 0 [(none, none, 0)] zo1 (.ok zo2) from .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable K0 [] zo3 := .write r2 (show Write3Step 0 [1, 3, 4] zo2 (.ok zo3) from .ok (by decide))
  have h4 : TransferStep K0 1 9 zo3 (.ok zo4) := .ok (by decide)
  have h5 : TransferStep K0 2 6 zo4 (.ok zo5) := .ok (by decide)
  exact ⟨.transfer (.transfer r3 h4) h5, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    .reject (by decide), by decide, h4, h5, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

#print axioms order_rejects_owned

theorem transfer_field_by_field :
    Reachable K0 [] pf1 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 3 pf0 .reject ∧ SameShape pf0.P 0 3 ∧
      TransferStep K0 1 4 pf0 (.ok pf1) ∧ Read3Step 1 [4] pf1 (.ok pf1) ∧
      Read3Step 1 [5] pf1 .reject := by
  have ht : TransferStep K0 1 4 pf0 (.ok pf1) := .ok (by decide)
  exact ⟨.transfer (.write (.enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)))
    (show Write3Step 0 [1] _ (.ok pf0) from .ok (by decide))) ht, .reject (by decide), by decide,
    ht, .ok (by decide), .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- J1, « sous-arbres isomorphes », read as an ordered isomorphism (`SameShape`: children matched
in index order); a question of the pass-8 report. Frame 1: structure 0 with the leaf 1 and the
structure 2 of fields 3 and 4; structure 5 with the structure 6 of fields 7 and 8, then the leaf 9;
structure 10 with the leaf 11 and the structure 12 of fields 13 and 14. The frame writes the leaves
of 0. The transfer of 0 into 5, isomorphic as unordered trees only, is rejected, by the shape
clause alone; into 10 (twin), accepted. Field by field, 1 into 9 and 2 into 6 have the same
shape. -/
def sq0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (some 2, none, 0),
  (some 2, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (some 5, none, 0), (some 6, none, 0), (some 6, none, 0),
  (some 5, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (some 10, none, 0), (some 10, none, 0), (some 12, none, 0),
  (some 12, none, 0)]
def sq1 : S3 := write3Eff sq0 [1, 3, 4]
theorem transfer_shape_ordered :
    Reachable K0 [] sq1 ∧ kids sq1.P 0 = [1, 2] ∧ kids sq1.P 5 = [6, 9] ∧
      ¬ SameShape sq1.P 0 5 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 5 sq1 .reject ∧
      (SameShape sq1.P 0 5 → TransferPre K0 sq1 0 5) ∧
      TransferStep K0 0 10 sq1 (.ok (transferEff sq1 0 10)) ∧
      SameShape sq1.P 1 9 ∧ SameShape sq1.P 2 6 := by
  exact ⟨.write (.enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)))
    (show Write3Step 0 [1, 3, 4] sq0 (.ok sq1) from .ok (by decide)), by decide, by decide,
    by decide, .reject (by decide), by decide, .ok (by decide), by decide, by decide⟩

/-- J1, bullets 2 and 3: an `issue` to a leaf of the arena value that is not `Init` makes it
`Init`, so the initialisation of the arena value changes (a question of the pass-8 report). Frame 1:
structure 0 with the fields 1 and 2, the arena value; 3 the allocator value; 4 a leaf. `alloc` gives
the storage 5 with the part 6, owned by 0. The frame writes 1 and 2, registers the arena
(`newArena 5 3`), moves the field 1 into 4 (1 becomes `Moved`), then issues `[6]` to 1: accepted,
1 is `Init` again. -/
def iv0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (none, none, 0),
  (none, none, 0)]
def iv1 : S3 := allocEff (write3Eff iv0 [3]) 3 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 5, none, 0)]
def iv1w : S3 := write3Eff iv1 [1, 2]
def iv2 : S3 := newArenaEff iv1w 5 3
def arIv : Arena := ⟨5, 3, [6], []⟩
def iv3 : S3 := transferEff iv2 1 4
def iv4 : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff iv3 arIv [6] 1).1 0 (issueEff iv3 arIv [6] 1).2
theorem issue_into_arena_value :
    Reachable K0 [] iv4 ∧ arenaValue iv3 arIv = some 0 ∧ 1 ∈ footprint iv3.P 0 ∧
      iv2.I 1 = .init ∧ iv3.I 1 = .moved ∧ IssueAt K0 0 0 [6] 1 iv3 (.ok iv4) ∧ iv4.I 1 = .init := by
  have r0 : Reachable K0 [] iv0 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have r1 : Reachable K0 [] iv1 := .alloc (.write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [3] iv0 (.ok _) from
    .ok (by decide))) (show AllocStep K0 3 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 5, none, 0)] _ (.ok iv1) from
      .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r2 : Reachable K0 [] iv2 := .newArena (.write r1 (show Write3Step 0 [1, 2] iv1 (.ok iv1w) from
    .ok (by decide))) (show NewArenaStep 5 3 iv1w (.ok iv2) from .ok (by decide))
  have r3 : Reachable K0 [] iv3 := .transfer r2 (show TransferStep K0 1 4 iv2 (.ok iv3) from
    .ok (by decide))
  have hi : IssueAt K0 0 0 [6] 1 iv3 (.ok iv4) :=
    .ok (ar := arIv) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
  exact ⟨.issue r3 hi, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, hi, by decide⟩

def cq5 : S3 := newArenaEff cq4 5 5
def arCq2 : Arena := ⟨5, 5, [5], []⟩

      ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (releaseEff cq5 5) (.ok (resetAtEff (releaseEff cq5 5) 0)) ∧
      IssueAt K0 1 0 [5] 3 (releaseEff cq5 5) .reject := by

  have r1 : Reachable K0 [] (write3Eff cq0 [1]) :=
    .write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [1] cq0 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable K0 [] cq2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep K0 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)] _ (.ok cq2) from .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable K0 [] cq3 := .newArena (.write r2 (show Write3Step 0 [0] cq2 (.ok cq2w) from

  have r4 : Reachable K0 [] cq4 := .issue r3 (show IssueAt K0 0 0 [5] 2 cq3 (.ok cq4) from

  have r5 : Reachable K0 [] cq5 := .newArena r4 (show NewArenaStep 5 5 cq4 (.ok cq5) from

/-- Right to update the metadata of the arena (A10; C6, aligned with `ProviderRight`): exercisable
`Modify` on the arena value, or an authority `via` exercisable at `Observe` (B2) with a present
effective mode on every metadata leaf, all `SharedMutable` (a `writeShared`, A9), with valid
dependencies. -/
def MetaRight (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s ar) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False ∨
  (s.ExercisableAt via .observe ∧ arenaValue s ar ≠ none ∧
    ∀ l ∈ metaLeaves s ar, effective s via l ≠ none ∧ k.SharedMutable l ∧ DepsValid s l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :
    Decidable (MetaRight k s ar via) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.issue(region)` (MM-03.3 §6; A10; J1): a `Modify` block derived from `internal`
on the region, held by the destination leaf; that leaf, and it only, becomes `Init` (J1, second
bullet), so the initialisation of the arena value is unchanged unless the destination is one of its
leaves (`issue_into_arena_value`; J1, third bullet: a question of the pass-8 report); the region
leaves `available` and joins `issued`. -/
def issueEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 × Arena :=
  ({ s.addAuth ⟨.modify, some ar.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩ with
      I := fun l => if l = dst then .init else s.I l },
   { ar with
      available := ar.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
      issued := (region, s.A.length) :: ar.issued })

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :

def resetEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : S3 × Arena :=

content.content:
- Rejet : aucun survivant sur la chaîne. Cela couvre « la chaîne atteint la racine d'un emplacement du cadre sortant », et aussi une racine inactive d'un cadre survivant.
    - La chaîne est `ancs` : elle suit `origin` vers des identités strictement décroissantes et s'arrête au premier lien qui ne décroît pas. Elle est donc toujours finie (`reanchor_terminates`). Sous l'ordre des origines de `WF3`, elle atteint une autorité sans origine (`reanchor_reaches_root`). Sans cet ordre, elle peut s'arrêter sur une autorité qui a encore une origine.
13. **`writeShared` (A9).** Le module exige une autorité exerçable et, sur chaque feuille, un mode effectif présent (`Observe` ou `Modify`), une feuille `SharedMutable` et des dépendances valides. L'effet met les feuilles à `Init`, comme `write3`. Les mots « depuis une autorité `Observe` » sont lus comme un minimum : une autorité `Modify` y est aussi admise.
14. **Arène (A10).**
    - La valeur arène est le propriétaire du stockage (`arenaValue`). Les métadonnées sont les feuilles de cette valeur (`metaLeaves`).
    - Le droit sur les métadonnées (`MetaRight`) est un droit `writeShared` : autorité exerçable, mode effectif présent, feuilles `SharedMutable`, dépendances valides.
    - `issue` exige ce droit, `internal` active, la région dans l'empreinte de `internal`, et une destination utilisable, sous `Modify` exerçable, sans feuille `Init`.
    - Issues de `issue` : une région hors de `available` donne `fail` ; une région disponible sur laquelle `internal` n'a pas `Modify` effectif donne `reject` (constructeur `noRight`) ; un échec d'une précondition statique donne `reject`.
    - `issue` n'installe aucune dépendance. A10 : « dépendants ancrés sur le bloc » ; un dépendant s'ancre sur le bloc par `depend`.
    - `reset` met les métadonnées à `Init`, rend toute l'empreinte de `internal` disponible et vide `issued`.
15. **`WF3` (A1).** Clauses, toutes hors du texte de MM-03.3 :
    - les origines précèdent leurs dérivées ;
    - les empreintes sont faites d'emplacements existants ;
    - la pile est non vide, sans doublon, sous `nF` ;
    - les cadres propriétaires sont sous `nF` ;
    - les emplacements propriétaires existent ;
----
64:| 7 | G2 | mineur | la valeur arène devient lisible sans écriture, par les métadonnées de `issue` et `reset` | légitime selon le relecteur (écriture des métadonnées sous `MetaRight`, §6 et §5) ; rien de changé, noté en (j) |
